title: Power of Two
description: Given an integer `n`, return `true` if it is a power of two. Otherwise, return `false`.
output_format: true if power of two, false otherwise.
hints: A power of two in binary has exactly one '1' bit (e.g. 1000...00).
Subtracting 1 flips all bits up to that 1 (e.g. 0111...11).
Therefore, `n & (n - 1) == 0` for all positive powers of two.

reference_solution:
import sys
data = sys.stdin.read().split()
if data:
    n = int(data[0])
    print('true' if n > 0 and (n & (n - 1)) == 0 else 'false')
